sections.h2: Who handles property tax in Cook County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Two courthouse offices share the work in Cook County: the County Assessor sets values and classifications, and the Auditor-Treasurer bills and collects the tax. Both sit in the county courthouse at 411 W. 2nd Street in Grand Marais, the county seat.

Call the Assessor at 218-387-3650 for anything about a value, a classification, a homestead filing or an inspection. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 about a bill, a payment or delinquent years. Current-year taxes can be paid through the county's online portal once the amounts are calculated in late March, but the county says delinquent taxes for prior years cannot be paid online.

sections.h2: What should a seller know about Cook County, Minnesota?
sections.html:
Cook County is the easternmost county in Minnesota, a rugged, heavily wooded triangle on the Lake Superior shore that reaches the Canadian border. It covers 1,452.57 square miles of land and had about 5,522 residents on the Census Bureau's July 2025 estimate, which works out to roughly four people per square mile.

  • Towns and communities on the county's own roster include Grand Marais, Hovland, Grand Portage, Tofte, Schroeder and Lutsen.
  • The Census Bureau counts 6,251 housing units but only 2,710 households, and the 2020 census found 54.3% of housing units vacant, a sign of how many cabins and second homes sit in the stock.
  • Owners occupy 77.7% of the homes lived in year-round, and the median value of those homes is $336,200 (2020 to 2024).
  • Median household income is $72,638, and 35.3% of residents are 65 or older.

The county is also the state's second-largest by area, 57% of its 3,340 square miles is water, and the Grand Portage Indian Reservation lies inside it. The highest natural point in Minnesota, Eagle Mountain at 2,301 feet, is here, and the county sits next to only one other county by land. About a third of the year (116 days) falls below freezing, according to the Wikipedia article on the county.

For a seller, those numbers mean the buyer pool is small and often seasonal, so taxes on a cabin or a lakeshore lot can differ a lot from a year-round house in town. Pull the current tax statement before you set a price.

sections.h2: When are Cook County property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Real estate tax is paid in two halves: the first by May 15 and the second by October 15, and the Cook County assessor's calendar lists November 15 as the second-half date for agricultural land. Both 2026 real estate dates have passed, so any unpaid half is already accruing penalty.

Minnesota Statutes section 279.01 sets the penalty: 2% on homestead property and 4% on nonhomestead property the day after a due date, with an added step on the first of the next month and then 1% each month, up to 8% for homestead and 12% for nonhomestead. The Auditor-Treasurer's office can tell you the exact payoff for each tax year.

  • Taxes of $100 or less are due in one payment on the first-half date.
  • If the statement was not postmarked before April 25, the first-half date moves to 21 days after the postmark.
  • The treasurer must waive the late penalty once for an owner whose mailed payment is postmarked within one business day of the due date.
  • A homeowner on federal active service as a National Guard or reserve member gets a four-month grace period, with a signed copy of orders attached.

If you are selling, ask that office for a payoff figure for the day of closing, because the county, not the title company, holds the final number for each parcel.

sections.h2: What does the Cook County assessment calendar look like?
sections.html:
The assessor's yearly calendar runs on fixed dates, and the ones below matter most to a homeowner or a seller timing a listing.

Selected Cook County, MN property tax dates (Cook County Assessor calendar)
DateWhat happens
January 2Assessment date for real and personal property
On or before March 31Auditor-Treasurer mails tax statements
March to MayAssessor mails market value notices, at least 10 days before the local board meets
April 1 to May 31Local boards of appeal and equalization meet
April 30Last day to file a Tax Court petition on current taxes
May 15 and October 15First and second half of real property tax due
Last 10 meeting days of June after the second FridayCounty Board of Appeal and Equalization convenes
November 24 (on or before)Notices of proposed taxes mailed
December 31Homestead and disabled veteran applications due

sections.h2: How do you dispute a valuation in Cook County?
sections.html:
Start by calling the assessor, and only after that go to the Cook County Board of Appeal and Equalization. The county's board notice says you must book an appointment to present an appeal, and that you may send written comments for the assessor to read for you if you cannot attend.

  • Gather sales of similar homes, an appraisal, or repair estimates that show a condition problem the assessor could not see.
  • Phone 218-387-3650 before the board meets, since many disagreements end at the assessor's desk.
  • Check the notice of valuation for the meeting date, because the county board meets in June.
  • If the board does not settle it, a petition to the Minnesota Tax Court or district court is the next step, and under section 278.01 the petition and proof of service must be filed by April 30 of the year the tax is payable.

The assessor also inspects each property at least once every five years. For the 2026 review cycle, which feeds the January 2, 2027 assessment, the area is Lutsen, Tofte and Schroeder, and the office takes appointments for those visits.

sections.h2: What happens to the tax bill when you sell a Cook County house?
sections.html:
A deed cannot be recorded until the Auditor-Treasurer confirms that no delinquent tax is owed on the land. Under section 272.12 the auditor checks the records, and the recorder will not accept the deed without the note "no delinquent taxes and transfer entered."

Two other filings go with a sale. A certificate of real estate value is required when the price is above $3,000 (section 272.115), and if the deed splits off part of a tax parcel, the treasurer must also certify that the current year's tax on the whole parcel is paid (section 272.121). The sale also ends the seller's homestead: the assessor removes homestead classification for the next assessment year unless the buyer files a homestead application and qualifies.

Ask the Auditor-Treasurer which years are open before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: Which Cook County tax relief programs have dates to watch?
sections.html:
The assessor's calendar flags several filing dates that a seller or new owner can miss. A homestead application must reach the assessor by December 31 to count for the next year's taxes, and the same date applies to the disabled veteran exclusion. Blind or permanently and totally disabled owners have until October 1 for the special homestead class, and the senior citizen property tax deferral request is due July 1.

The Property Tax Refund form M-1PR is due August 15 under the same calendar. Resort owners have a January 15 declaration, and managed forest land under the 2c classification has an April 30 application date. Ask the assessor which of these fit your parcel.

faqs.q: Is this the same Cook County as Chicago?
faqs.a: No. This page covers Cook County, Minnesota, on the north shore of Lake Superior, with Grand Marais as county seat. Its property tax offices are the Assessor at 218-387-3650 and the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640.

faqs.q: When is the next Cook County property tax payment due?
faqs.a: The 2026 halves, May 15 and October 15, are past, so the next real estate date is the first-half deadline in May 2027, for taxes payable in 2027. Agricultural land used November 15 for its second half this year. Statements are mailed on or before March 31.

faqs.q: Can I pay delinquent Cook County taxes online?
faqs.a: No. The county says delinquent taxes for prior years cannot be paid online, only current-year taxes once the amounts are calculated in late March. Call the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 to get a payoff amount.

faqs.q: Can I still appeal my Cook County value this year?
faqs.a: The 2026 local and county board meetings are over. A Tax Court or district court petition on taxes payable in 2027 must be filed by April 30, 2027, and you should talk to the assessor first. Call 218-387-3650.

faqs.q: Do I have to pay off the tax before selling a Cook County house?
faqs.a: Delinquent tax must be cleared before the deed can be recorded, and the auditor stamps the deed once that is done. Ask the Auditor-Treasurer at 218-387-3640 for the amount owed on your parcel before you accept an offer.
